title: Stroke sculpting as a DSL: stroke_sculpt reads each pass's SVG, passes chain as nodes, with a symmetry axis and stroke-driven refinement

description:
Follow-up to MESH-68 (stroke sculpting, landed). Turn the sculpt into a plain DSL: each pass is a stroke_sculpt node that reads that pass's SVG directly, and passes are chained nodes rebuilt from the sphere on every run. This replaces rounds stored to and loaded from cage files:

  ball = sphere(...)
  p1 = stroke_sculpt(geometry=ball.mesh, svg="skull/pass1.svg", symmetry="x")
  p2 = stroke_sculpt(geometry=p1.geometry, svg="skull/pass2.svg", symmetry="x")
  smooth = subdivision_surface(geometry=p2.geometry, levels=2)

Design:
1. The SVG carries the camera it was drawn with. When a multiview is captured for drawing, its center, distance, cell size and view table are written onto the <svg> root (e.g. data-center, data-distance). The node lifts through that fixed camera, not one re-framed on the current mesh, so re-running the DSL lifts the same pixels the same way.
2. Headless lifting. The node casts CPU rays against its input mesh using Camera3D math. It does not need the viewer, so the DSL runs headless and under BatchDslEvaluator / dsl_optimizer. The stroke-lift route stays as a preview of where strokes would land and shares the node's lift code.
3. Strokes are re-lifted onto the node's input mesh on every run, so editing an earlier pass carries the later passes along. A lift-once anchored mode is out of scope unless drift proves a problem.
4. The base/store ports go, and so does SculptCageFile; the DSL is the whole sculpt. SilhouetteDrag has a single user (StrokeSculpt) and is folded into it (Ixdar CLAUDE.md: a class earns its file only as a named concept with behaviour or an identity that outlives its owner).
5. A strength parameter on the node (a multiplier on the pass) so dsl_optimizer can tune each pass against chamfer to a reference, while the agent decides where the strokes go.
6. A symmetry axis on the node: symmetry="x" (also y/z, default none). The agent struggled to keep the skull symmetric with per-stroke data-mirror. With symmetry set, every stroke of the pass is applied on both sides, and afterwards the pass's displacement is symmetrised: each vertex is averaged with the reflection of its mirror twin, the twins found by a KD-tree lookup of the reflected position. Requires a symmetric input cage (the welded sphere is). Per-stroke data-mirror stays for single strokes.
7. Stroke-driven local refinement (carried over from MESH-68, not done there). A stroke's stroke-width, and its gap to nearby strokes, converted to surface distance at the lift point, set the edge length needed. Before lifting, the node subdivides only the faces within the stroke's falloff region until their edges are below that length (about 1/3 of the stroke width). It closes T-junctions at the boundary with transition triangles and carries crease marks onto the split edges. Refinement is deterministic from the strokes, so re-running replays it. With symmetry set, the refinement is mirrored too. Goal: the skull's teeth become sculptable.
8. The animation steps node by node: each pass's SVG over the mesh going into it, then the mesh coming out, with chamfer to the goal per pass.
definition-of-done:
1. stroke_sculpt takes svg (a file path) and lifts it itself through the camera stored on the SVG root; ixdar-cli multiview can write that camera into a blank SVG template for the agent to draw on.
2. The node runs headless: evaluating a stroke DSL through BatchDslEvaluator (no viewer) gives the same mesh as the viewer does.
3. SculptCageFile, the base/store ports and SilhouetteDrag.java are gone; no new class in this change has a single user.
4. symmetry="x" on the node gives a result whose mirror distance (mean distance from each vertex to the nearest vertex of the reflected mesh) is below 1e-4 of the bounding diagonal.
5. Local refinement subdivides only around strokes and leaves no T-junctions or open boundary. A test pass carves a row of small bumps individually.
6. A demo chained-pass DSL on a self-made target (no goal mesh) under resources/dsl/, showing symmetry, refinement, and that editing pass 1 and re-running keeps pass 2; with a launch.json entry. The skull is rebuilt separately by a blind sculptor run (the stroke-sculpt skill), not in this ticket.
7. The animation tooling steps node by node, demonstrated on the demo DSL under tmp/.
testing-plan:
1. Lift one SVG headlessly and in the viewer; compare the vertex ids and positions they produce.
2. Edit pass 1's strengths and re-run; check pass 2 still applies and the result differs only as expected.
3. A one-sided stroke with symmetry="x": measure the mirror distance of the result.
4. Refinement: the stroke region's edge lengths drop below the target, the face count elsewhere is unchanged, and mesh-holes reports no new boundary loops.
5. Score the rebuilt skull DSL with mesh-compare against the full goal; then run dsl_optimizer over the strengths and score again.
unknowns: Does re-lifting later passes onto an edited earlier pass drift enough to need a lift-once anchored mode?
Does symmetrising after each pass fight silhouette strokes drawn on an asymmetric view (3/4 cells)?
changes-made: Built: StrokeSketch (geometry/mesh/data/sculpt) is a pass's drawing: the SVG plus the camera written on its root (data-center, data-distance, data-fov, data-projection, data-cell-width/height, data-columns, data-views). StrokeSketch.read resolves a path as a file, then under src/main/resources/, then on the classpath; lift(mesh) casts CPU rays through Camera3D (new overloads of updateProjection, rayThroughPixel and worldPerPixel that take the view size instead of reading the framebuffer) and a TriangleBvh over the mesh's fan triangles, Moller-Trumbore per leaf. Users: StrokeSculptNode, the stroke-lift route, MultiviewScreenshot (its attribute names) and the test. multiview --svg writes the blank template. stroke-lift now takes only svg (no multiview JSON) and previews on the shown mesh through the same code. SculptCageFile, SilhouetteDrag (folded into StrokeSculpt.apply), the base/store ports and the dangling stroke_sculpt_skull.dsl are gone. No new Java class has a single user.

Node: stroke_sculpt(geometry, svg, strokes, strength, symmetry, displace, scale, falloff, crease). strength multiplies the whole pass (displacement, drag, smoothing, crease); symmetry x/y/z reflects every stroke (silhouette eyes too), then averages each vertex's displacement with its mirror twin's reflected displacement, twins found by NearestVertex at the reflected position. Refinement: each stroke's target edge = max(0.005, min(falloff radius, mean gap to the nearest other source stroke) / 3); faces within a stroke's reach whose longest edge exceeds the smallest target at their corners split (quad to 4 quads, triangle to 4), then close: a whole face with one split edge gets transition triangles, a quad with two opposite split edges two quads, anything else splits too; up to 4 rounds; crease marks follow split edges; with symmetry the required length is min'd with the twin's so the split set mirrors exactly. Fills now take every vertex within the fill-sample spacing as a source, so a fill on a refined region is solid instead of spotted.

Verified (tmp/mesh70/): headless == viewer: BatchDslEvaluator OBJ of stroke_sculpt_head.dsl vs the viewer mesh, mesh-compare hausdorff 8.5e-7 (OBJ print precision), 34602 vertices both. Lift == viewer pick: stroke-lift points on the Front and Right cells equal ixdar-cli pick at the same pixel to 4 decimals. Symmetry: mirror distance / diagonal 8e-9 with symmetry=x, 5.2e-3 with none. Editing pass1_strength to 0.5 or 1.5 and re-running keeps passes 2 and 3 (same refinement, only the outline changes; tmp/mesh70/edit_pass1_strength_0.5_vs_1.5.png). Refinement: six teeth 14 px wide carve individually (tmp/mesh70/pass3_front.png); StrokeSculptTest checks edges under each tooth below a third of its width, faces behind the head unchanged and no boundary. Headless evaluation of the 3-pass head: 0.65 s per run including JVM start. The goal-mesh floor measured before the plan changed: 57k decimated skull vs an offset-grid 57k copy, chamfer 0.00216, Hausdorff 0.0046 (38k copy 0.00210, 150k copy 0.00154).

orbit-set gains fov (degrees) and roll (radians), kept when omitted, both reported; orbit-get reports roll. Camera3D.roll turns the up vector about the view axis in applyOrbit; positive turns the picture counter-clockwise (a roll +0.05 screenshot matches roll 0 after a 2.865 degree clockwise rotation, RMSE 0.29 vs 1.25 unrotated). onScroll no longer clamps a wider route-set fov back to 45. multiview zeroes roll for its capture and restores it, and records fov on the template. Screens: tmp/mesh70/orbit_fov_roll_grid.png (fov 25, fov 60, roll +0.05, roll -0.05).

Animation: ixdar-cli sculpt-animate --dsl X [--reference OBJ] writes, per stroke_sculpt node, the node's input captured through its SVG's camera with the strokes drawn over it, then the node's output (chamfer and Hausdorff when a reference is given), as frames plus animation.mp4/gif; stdlib plus ffmpeg (librsvg overlay, drawtext). Demo: tmp/mesh70/animation/. For a pictures-only sculptor: strengths are in units of scale=0.2 world, so a strength-0.6 valley 45 px wide is a pit deeper than it is wide; start features near 0.2-0.3. Every pass needs its own multiview --svg template captured from its input (the DSL ending at the previous pass). Chain strokes on a refined region zigzag along edges and read as knobbly ridges; fills read cleaner. Each stroke must lie in one cell. A refined cage shows its transition faces under curvature shading until subdivision_surface.
review-summary: The stroke_sculpt node now reads each pass's SVG and lifts it headlessly through the camera multiview writes on it, so sculpt passes chain as plain DSL nodes, with a pass strength, a symmetry axis and local refinement. F5 'MESH-70: mesh-viewer stroke sculpt head' opens a demo head.
